candidates.what_happened: Trump posted a White House graphic on Truth Social and Instagram claiming the former US childhood vaccine schedule called for '72 injections' versus '11' in a comparison European country -- rated False by PolitiFact, since the 72 figure covers 18 years of doses, many combined or oral, not 72 needle-sticks in infancy.

quotes.text: European Country: 11 injections. United States: 72 injections.
quotes.speaker: White House graphic posted by Donald Trump

candidates.reason: No video of Trump saying or presenting this exists -- it's a static graphic post, and searches returned only general CDC-policy news coverage, not the actual claim being made on camera. Cut for failing the video-of-the-moment requirement.

candidates.what_happened: Trump claimed 'we right now have more factories and plants being built in our country than we've ever had before' -- rated Half True by PolitiFact, which found construction spending on manufacturing facilities was elevated but not a clean all-time record by every measure.
candidates.reason: Half True rather than clearly false or absurd, no standout quote or visual moment, and yt-dlp search returned no relevant real-outlet video of the actual statement. Weakest comedic hook of the pool; cut.

candidates.what_happened: After a string of US military strikes on suspected drug vessels in the Caribbean and Pacific, Trump claimed drugs entering the country by sea are 'down 97%' -- rated False by PolitiFact against actual seizure and trafficking data.
candidates.reason: A false statistic but a dry one with no built-in punchline, and yt-dlp searches for the claim returned no relevant real-outlet video of Trump making it. Cut for weak video and weak comedic hook.

candidates.what_happened: Trump posted on Truth Social that credit card companies would be 'in violation of the law' if they didn't voluntarily cap interest rates at 10% by January 20 -- PolitiFact found no such law exists; Trump only later, at Davos on January 21, asked Congress to actually pass one.
